title: Compact weekly outcome dossier — 7 day sprint
content:
Context: quick personal log for a focused 7-day outcome sprint. This is raw — ideas, micro-experiments, a compact scorecard. Use as the single source for next-week planning.

Objectives (weekly):
- O1: Reduce my blocking PR review turnaround to <24h (impact: keeps infra launches on track)
- O2: Get a working prototype of the lightweight experiment harness for kernel selection (impact: sanity-check perf delta)
- O3: 3 quality prompt-evals for the optimizer recommendations (impact: prevent regression)

Northstar metrics (how I’ll judge progress this week):
- PR review TTR (median): baseline 36h -> target 24h (current: 28h)
- Harness prototype: baseline 0 -> target usable demo by Fri (current: alpha with stubbed kernels)
- Eval coverage: baseline 0 -> target 3 prompt sets (current: 1)

Scorecard (quick numbers):
- Days elapsed: 7
- PRs reviewed: 6 (2 large infra, 4 small fixes)
- TTR median this window: 28h (improved from 36h)
- Harness commits: 5 (lib scaffold + small simulation harness)
- Prompt evals run: 1/3 (ran regression smoke on top-k kernels)
- Meetings: 6 (2 syncs, 2 reviews, 1 retro, 1 onboarding)

What worked:
- Blocking reviews: setting a 90-minute daily review block reduced context switch cost. Felt focused.
- Kernel harness: the light harness (node-based driver + docker-in-docker job) let me iterate quickly without full infra. Saved ~1 day vs earlier approach.
- Quick eval: running a focused 10-sample smoke caught a prompt formatting regression early.

What didn’t work / blockers:
- Can’t reproduce slow path in simulation reliably. Perf diffs only show up under sustained 200 concurrent connections; my local harness doesn't emulate that.
- Two days lost to an unrelated oncall spike — need plan to protect sprint blocks.
- Prompt-eval automation flaky because of tokenization edge-case in the harness.

Hypotheses / micro-experiments for next sprint:
- H1: Adding a small synthetic load generator to the harness (simple goroutine worker pool) will surface the slow path without needing prod-scale infra. Accept if variance <10% vs canary run.
- H2: Locking a calendar focus block (3 x 90 min) prevents >24h review slips. Accept if median TTR <= 24h across next 2 weeks.
- H3: Normalizing prompt whitespace before tokenization will remove the tokenization flakiness. Accept if eval pass rate improves from 66% -> 95% on edge set.

Concrete next actions (priority-ordered):
1) Add synthetic load generator to harness (ETA: Tue) — minimal API, configurable concurrency and sequence length. Link stub: REDW-421.
2) Put persistent 90-min review block MWF on calendar and notify team (ETA: Today).
3) Implement prompt whitespace normalization and add test cases for existing failing prompts (ETA: Wed).
4) Run 3 prompt-eval suites against alpha harness; capture diffs and snapshot seeds (ETA: Fri).
5) Draft short retrospective note for the team re: review cadence + oncall shielding (ETA: Fri EOD).

Open questions / risks:
- If synthetic load doesn’t trigger the slow path, do we spend cycles spinning up a dedicated canary env? Cost/time tradeoff.
- How much time can I reallocate from project work to keep review TTR under 24h without harming deliverables?

Quick retro bullets (tone-for-team):
- Positive: review block reduced context switching and felt sustainable — would recommend to others doing deep infra work.
- Negative: oncall override model needs clearer guardrails for sprint-protected time.
- Ask: product team — can we flag low-latency review items so they don’t get deprioritized?

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep content of harness RFC minimal — it’s a prototype, not the final arch.
- Save perf artifacts (cpu profiles + logs) in short-date folder: /tmp/perf-20250917/
- When writing tests, include deterministic random seeds for all evals.

Mini-archive (links / quick refs):
- PRs to follow up: redwood/serving-runtime#842 (review), redwood/tools/harness#13 (prototype commit)
- Linear: REDW-421 (harness), REDW-522 (prompt-eval pipeline)

Mood / meta: feeling pragmatic. Small wins this week (PR TTR improved), but still a little reactive. Aim to defend next sprint focus blocks more aggressively.

End-of-sprint quick checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] synthetic load generator added
- [x] review block set on calendar
- [x] whitespace normalization PR opened (WIP)
- [ ] run all 3 prompt-eval suites
- [ ] draft team retro note

If I get time: sketch a short one-pager explaining why keeping median TTR low is high-leverage for infra launches (put in product sync).

-- marissa
